_note: Live seqId dispatch traces from the Citra JIT read-watch hook (effect_seq_hook.patch). seqId = (faulting_vaddr - Battle.cro rodata+0x45a0)/8, seqtbl VA 0x7de5a0 (base 0x6dd180). broad_table_watch._note: Watched a broad rodata span [0x7de000,0x7e4800) covering all four EFFECT_DISPATCH candidate tables (0x45a0/0x67b8/0x7e24/0x98ac) during move execution. FINDING: 0x45a0 is the shared MOVE-FLOW sequencer (core [6,11,5,4,62,65,22,23,58,28] runs for every damaging move, minor move-specific variation), NOT indexed by effectId. The larger tables (0x67b8/0x7e24/0x98ac) are touched only SPARSELY (single reads) at inconsistent large indices that differ by move/state (Steam eff4 -> 0x7e24[339]; Hydro eff0 -> 0x67b8[399]) -- NO clean effectId->index mapping. Consistent with the earlier static disproof. Conclusion: the effectId->seqId 'remap' is NOT a clean single-table lookup; the move effect is applied data-driven within the shared move-flow handlers, consuming the already-extracted move-effect DATA (usum_moves.json status/statChanges/flags/effectId).

category_dispatch_DECISIVE._note: DECISIVE non-KO capture (0-power 100%-effect status moves poked into the lead's battlemon move-records via /tmp/poke, target survives so the effect always applies; broad watch over rodata [0x7de000,0x7e4800]). The move-effect dispatch IS in the 0x45a0 table but keyed by effect CATEGORY, not per-effectId: seqId 80 = inflict status (burn/sleep/confuse), 71 = stat-change on TARGET, 70 = stat-change on SELF (each +a message/anim sub-step 31/43/41). The specific status/stat/stages are data-driven from usum_moves.json (already extracted). This overturns the earlier 'no clean table' reading (an artifact of KO-masking).
